nindian-polity-2-53.s:
Consider the following statements about the Emergency Articles:
1. Article 359 deals with the duty of the Union to protect the States.
2. Article 354 deals with the distribution of revenues during an Emergency.
3. Article 358 deals with the suspension of Article 19 during an Emergency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nindian-polity-2-53.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Article 359 deals with suspension of enforcement of Fundamental Rights; the Union's duty to protect the States is Article 355.

n4e8fbdbac25.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Polavaram project?
o: Its national-project status comes from the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
It is fully funded by the Centre
It was declared a national project under Section 89 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
n4e8fbdbac25.x: Polavaram is a national project under Section 90, not Section 89, of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, and is fully Centre-funded.

n5b1af0fbf90.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a Financial Emergency?
o: The Constitution prescribes no maximum period for it
It has been proclaimed several times in India
n5b1af0fbf90.x: A Financial Emergency has never been declared in India; it has no maximum period and continues until revoked.

nindian-polity-44-14.s: A vacancy in the office of the President caused by death, resignation or removal must be filled within:
nindian-polity-44-14.x: An election to fill such a vacancy must be held within six months; meanwhile the Vice-President acts as President.

nindian-polity-44-26.s: A Proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by Parliament within:
nindian-polity-44-26.x: President's Rule needs parliamentary approval within two months; the one-month limit applies to a National Emergency.

nindian-polity-50-11.s: Article 359 provides for the suspension of:
o: The six freedoms of Article 19 automatically
The distribution of revenues between Union and States
The term of the Lok Sabha
The right to move courts to enforce specified Fundamental Rights
nindian-polity-50-11.x: Article 359 suspends the right to approach courts for specified Fundamental Rights, in external emergencies and in armed rebellion.

nindian-polity-15-21.s: The principle that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but cannot destroy the Basic Structure was laid down in:
nindian-polity-15-21.x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but not the basic structure of the Constitution.

n58a4b5e8259.s: Which provision lets Parliament bar the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts over inter-State river water disputes?
n58a4b5e8259.x: Article 262(2) lets Parliament bar court jurisdiction over water disputes, so Article 131 does not cover them; 262(1) provides for their adjudication.

n716f806d024.s: Which of the following pairs about the Inter-State Council is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Union Cabinet Ministers – six, nominated by the Prime Minister
Governors – permanent members for all States
Standing Committee chair – Union Home Minister
n716f806d024.x: Governors are members only for States under President's Rule, not permanent members for all States.

nb6a03bc73be.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Zonal Councils?
o: Chief Ministers act as Vice-Chairmen by annual rotation
Their recommendations are legally binding on the States
They are deliberative and advisory bodies
Each is chaired by the Union Home Minister
nb6a03bc73be.x: Zonal Councils are advisory; their recommendations are not binding on the States.

n9f14f73c958.s: The Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal involves which States?
n9f14f73c958.x: The Vansadhara Tribunal (2010) concerns Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

new.s: The Sarkaria Commission on Union-State relations was formed on:
new.x: The Sarkaria Commission, chaired by Justice R.S. Sarkaria, was formed on 9 June 1983.

new.s: Legislative relations between the Union and the States are covered by Articles:
new.x: Part XI covers legislative relations in Articles 245-255 and administrative relations in Articles 256-263.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional scheme of Centre-State relations:
1. Part XI covers legislative and administrative relations.
2. Part XII covers financial relations in Articles 268-293.
3. Administrative relations are dealt with in Part XII.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Administrative relations are in Part XI (Articles 256-263), so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the effects of a National Emergency on Centre-State relations?
o: Laws made under Article 250 end six months after the Emergency ends
Cuts in transfers under Article 354 last till the end of that financial year
Under Article 353, State Governments are suspended
The Lok Sabha term can be extended by one year at a time
new.x: Under Article 353 the Union may direct a State on any matter, but State Governments are not suspended.

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a Financial Emergency?
new.x: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency; 352 is National Emergency and 356 President's Rule.

new.s: Under Article 365, a State's failure to comply with Union directions may be treated as:
new.x: Article 365 treats defiance of Union directions as a breakdown of constitutional machinery, opening the way to Article 356.

new.s: The IMDT Act, 1983 was struck down for violating Article 355 in:
o: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India
Sarbananda Sonowal v. Union of India (2005)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
new.x: The Supreme Court struck down the IMDT Act in Sarbananda Sonowal v. Union of India (2005) for violating Article 355.

new.s: The CBI needs the consent of a State to operate there under:
new.x: State consent for the CBI is required by Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act; Article 156 concerns the Governor.

new.s: The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President under Article:
new.x: Under Article 156 the Governor holds office at the President's pleasure, a recurring source of Centre-State friction.

new.s: The Centre fixes a Net Borrowing Ceiling for States under Article:
new.x: The Net Borrowing Ceiling (about 3% of GSDP) is fixed under Article 293.

new.s: In April 2024, Kerala's suit against borrowing limits under Article 131 was referred to a:
new.x: Kerala's Article 131 suit on the borrowing ceiling was referred to a five-judge bench in April 2024.

new.s: The Budget 2026-27 allocation for Polavaram provides storage up to what height?
new.x: Budget 2026-27 gave Rs 3,320 crore for storage up to 41.15 m, against the demand for the full 45.72 m.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was promised in Parliament by PM Manmohan Singh.
2. It was written into the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
3. It means 90% central funding of Centrally Sponsored Schemes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: SCS was promised by Manmohan Singh and means 90% CSS funding, but it was never written into the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

new.s: The suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency is borrowed from the:
new.x: Suspension of Fundamental Rights in an Emergency comes from the Weimar Constitution; the emergency provisions as such come from the 1935 Act.

new.s: The emergency provisions (Articles 352-360) are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
new.x: Emergency provisions are in Part XVIII, Articles 352-360.

new.s: The President must revoke a National Emergency if the Lok Sabha passes a resolution disapproving it by a:
new.x: Disapproval by the Lok Sabha needs only a simple majority, after which the President must revoke the proclamation.

new.s: The first National Emergency, proclaimed in 1962, was due to:
new.x: The 1962 Emergency followed Chinese aggression; 1971 was the Indo-Pak war and 1975 internal disturbance.

new.s: During President's Rule in a State, the powers of the High Court:
new.x: The President cannot assume or suspend the powers of the High Court; it is untouched by President's Rule.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about President's Rule under Article 356:
1. It may be imposed on the Governor's report or otherwise.
2. It needs the consent of the State Legislature.
3. Each parliamentary approval keeps it in force for six months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: President's Rule needs no State Legislature consent; it may be imposed on the Governor's report or otherwise, and each approval lasts six months.

new.s: During President's Rule, laws for the State are made by:
new.x: The Assembly is suspended or dissolved and Parliament legislates for the State (or delegates that power to the President).

new.s: Which Article imposes the Union's duty to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance, the basis of Article 356?
new.x: Article 355 lays down this duty and forms the basis of President's Rule under Article 356.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 365:
1. It lets the President hold that constitutional machinery has failed when a State does not comply with Union directions.
2. It imposes on the Union the duty to protect States against external aggression.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 describes Article 365; the duty to protect States is Article 355.

new.s: Which States have never been under President's Rule?
new.x: Chhattisgarh and Telangana have never been under President's Rule; Manipur and UP have had it most often.

new.s: Which State has been placed under President's Rule the most times?
new.x: Manipur has had President's Rule 11 times (the 11th in February 2025); Uttar Pradesh follows with 10.

new.s: The second spell of President's Rule in Andhra Pradesh (March-June 2014) followed the resignation of Chief Minister:
new.x: CM Kiran Kumar Reddy resigned over bifurcation, leading to President's Rule from 1 March to 8 June 2014.

new.s: During a Financial Emergency, the salaries that may be reduced include those of:
o: All government servants, including Supreme Court and High Court judges
new.x: Under a Financial Emergency the salaries of all government servants, including SC and HC judges, can be cut.

new.s: During a Financial Emergency, Money Bills and Financial Bills passed by a State Legislature may be:
o: Returned to the Governor for reconsideration
Reserved for the consideration of the President
new.x: The Union may require State Money and Financial Bills to be reserved for the President during a Financial Emergency.

new.s: Which amendment made the President's satisfaction in proclaiming an Emergency non-justiciable?
new.x: The 38th Amendment made the satisfaction non-justiciable; this was later reversed.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a change made by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978?
o: Cut the approval period to one month
new.x: Making the President's satisfaction non-justiciable was done by the 38th Amendment (1975); the 44th made the other three changes.

new.s: The 42nd Amendment (1976) raised the term of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies to:
new.x: The 42nd Amendment, the 'mini-constitution', raised these terms to 6 years.

new.s: Under Article 261(3), final judgments or orders of civil courts:
o: Can be executed only within the State concerned
Can be executed anywhere in India according to law
Need confirmation by the Supreme Court
Need the President's sanction for execution
new.x: Article 261(3) makes final civil court judgments and orders executable anywhere in India according to law.

new.s: Under Article 261(2), the manner of proof of public acts and records and their effect is decided by:
new.x: Article 261(2) leaves the manner of proof and effect to Parliament by law.

new.s: Which Article allows Parliament to restrict trade, commerce and intercourse in the public interest?
new.x: Article 302 lets Parliament impose restrictions in the public interest; Article 301 guarantees the freedom.

new.s: Which Article of Part XIII, relating to Part B States, has been repealed?
new.x: Article 306 on Part B States was repealed; Article 307 provides an authority for Articles 301-304.

new.s: The Inter-State Council decides all questions by:
new.x: The Inter-State Council decides all questions by consensus and meets in camera.

new.s: Each Zonal Council is chaired by the:
o: Chief Minister of the host State by rotation
new.x: The Union Home Minister chairs every Zonal Council; a Chief Minister acts as Vice-Chairman by rotation.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Zonal Councils:
1. They were set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
2. There are five Zonal Councils.
3. They are constitutional bodies under Article 263.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Zonal Councils are five statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, not constitutional bodies.

new.s: The 29th meeting of the Southern Zonal Council was held at:
new.x: The 29th Southern Zonal Council meeting was held at Tirupati, chaired by Amit Shah.

new.s: The North Eastern Council was set up under the:
new.x: The NEC is a statutory body under the North Eastern Council Act, 1971.

new.s: Which State became the eighth member of the North Eastern Council through the 2002 amendment?
new.x: The 2002 amendment added Sikkim as the 8th member State and made the NEC a regional planning body.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the North Eastern Council?
o: The Union Home Minister is its Chairman
The Minister of DoNER is its Vice-Chairman
The President nominates three of its members
It is a constitutional body under Article 263
new.x: The NEC is statutory, set up under the NEC Act, 1971, not a constitutional body.

new.s: Which of the following is a constitutional body?
new.x: The Inter-State Council rests on Article 263; Zonal Councils and the NEC are statutory and the NDC is non-statutory.

new.s: The National Development Council is a non-constitutional, non-statutory body created by:
new.x: The NDC was created by an executive resolution, so it is neither constitutional nor statutory.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263, not a statutory one.

new.s: Under which law has no board ever been set up?
new.x: No board has ever been set up under the River Boards Act, 1956 (not 1970).

new.s: The Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal was set up in:
new.x: The Cauvery Tribunal (Karnataka, Kerala, TN, Puducherry) was set up in 1990.

new.s: The ad hoc division of Krishna water between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana from 2014-15 is:
new.x: KWDT-I's 811 tmcft for undivided AP is shared 512 (AP) : 299 (Telangana), a 66:34 ratio.

new.s: How much Krishna water did KWDT-I allot to undivided Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: KWDT-I allotted 811 tmcft to undivided AP; 968 tmcft is the Godavari figure AP disputes.
